Select Edges for an Embedding Plot

Source: R/overlays.R
embed_edges.Rd

Prepare an ordinary edge table for the overlays argument of embed_plot(), embed_ggplot() or embed_plotly().

Usage

embed_edges(x, select = "all", k = NULL)

Arguments

x

A list with a ranked neighbor index matrix idx and optional matching distance matrix dist. Row and neighbor IDs refer to the same observations. Examples include a uwot metric block (fit$nn[[1]]) and a neighbor graph returned by rnndescent. Alternatively, supply a square, symmetric numeric sparse Matrix, such as a uwot fit$fgraph.

select

For ranked neighbors, "all", "nearest" (rank one), or "furthest" (the last retained input-space neighbor in each row). Sparse graphs support only "all" because directional ranks are lost.

k

Optional positive integer. With "all", keep up to the first k non-self neighbors per row. With "furthest", take exactly rank k; every row must have that many neighbors.

Value

A data frame with integer columns from and to indexing rows of the original coordinates. Ranked input contributes directed edges with rank and, if supplied, distance. Sparse input contributes a single undirected edge per nonzero above the diagonal, with its value as weight. The n_vertices attribute records the input observation count.

Details

Ranked indices are one-based and distances must be nondecreasing within each row. Every occurrence of self is removed by ID. Other IDs retain their first occurrence, including distinct neighbors tied at zero distance. uwot normally counts self in its requested neighbor count.

Examples

nn <- list(idx = rbind(c(1, 2, 3), c(2, 1, 3), c(3, 2, 1)))
edges <- embed_edges(nn, select = "nearest")
embed_plot(cbind(1:3, c(1, 3, 2)), colors = "navy", overlays = edges)
